s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement and discomfort of a digit with associated neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been larger than the others since birth
The finger has grown progressively over time
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
There is limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
The overlying skin of the enlarged finger is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
Sensation is decreased distally
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
A CT scan of the hand showed overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue

shortlist.label: Macrodactyly
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive enlargement of the finger since birth

shortlist.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showing lipomatous process and overgrowth of phalanges

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Neurological symptoms such as tingling and decreased sensation

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive enlargement and associated neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and lipomatous process

raw.rationale: The patient's condition is characterized by an enlarged finger since birth with progressive growth, limited flexion, and decreased sensation, which are all consistent with macrodactyly, a condition involving abnormal overgrowth of a digit.

rejected.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: While the CT scan suggests a lipomatous process, lipofibromatous hamartoma typically involves nerve tissue and may not fully explain the progressive overgrowth of the digit.

rejected.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
rejected.why: There is no mention of other characteristic features such as café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, or a family history of the condition.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically involves a triad of port-wine stain, varicose veins or other vascular anomalies, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, none of which are mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Similar to lipofibromatous hamartoma, fibrolipomatous hamartoma involves nerve tissue and may not fully explain the clinical presentation of progressive macrodactyly.
